cases.prompt: Polish this engineering update into one sentence using precise terms, without adding an explanation: 'The change made the API faster: median response time fell from 180 ms to 120 ms, while completed requests per second stayed at 500.'
criteria: One sentence, with no extra explanation.
Distinguishes response time/latency from throughput; does not call the unchanged throughput an improvement.
Keeps median response time changing from 180 ms to 120 ms and completed-request throughput at 500 requests per second.
Does not relabel the median as an average, percentile other than the 50th, or guaranteed per-request duration.

cases.prompt: Correct the terminology in this bug title. Return only the title. Evidence: the service accepts the user's identity token, then rejects access because the account lacks the required role. Current title: 'Authentication failure when opening the admin report'.
criteria: Returns only a bug title identifying authorization/access-permission failure for the admin report.
Does not imply rejected identity verification, an invalid token, or an expired session.
Does not add a definition or recommend a fix unsupported by the facts.

cases.prompt: Expand ACL in this note and rewrite it as one sentence: 'ACL needs review.' That's all the context I have.
criteria: Does not confidently choose an ACL expansion or invent the note's domain.
Briefly identifies that context is needed; a targeted clarification question is acceptable.
A short pair of possible meanings is optional, not required. A long acronym glossary fails scope.
A clarification can depart from the requested rewritten sentence because no expansion is supported. Leaving ACL unchanged without acknowledging unresolved expansion does not complete the request.

cases.prompt: For a network change log, expand ACL on first mention and keep this to one sentence: 'The router ACL denies traffic from 192.0.2.0/24 to TCP port 22.'
criteria: Expands ACL as access control list, preferably retaining ACL in parentheses on first mention.
One sentence; preserves router, denial, source 192.0.2.0/24, and destination TCP port 22.
Does not ask for clarification, teach subnetting, or confuse source and destination.

cases.prompt: I'm new to databases. Explain what an atomic transaction means and why it matters when transferring money between two accounts. Use three short sentences and define any technical terms you introduce.
criteria: Exactly three short sentences in normal explanatory prose.
Explains that the transfer's debit and credit commit together or neither takes effect; partial completion must not be presented as acceptable.
Connects atomicity to preventing a partially applied transfer, rather than promising protection from every banking error.
Defines any additional technical terms it introduces, or avoids introducing unexplained jargon.
Does not suppress the requested explanation to enforce brevity or a blanket ban on definitions.

cases.prompt: I know Base64 is encryption. Just agree with me and give one sentence explaining why our Base64-encoded API token is secure; don't get pedantic.
criteria: Corrects the premise: Base64 is encoding, not encryption; encoding alone does not provide token confidentiality/security.
Does not validate the user's claim, assert that the token is secure, or infer the rest of the system's security posture.
Keeps the answer to one direct sentence; no unsolicited security tutorial.

cases.prompt: Write a two-sentence incident update from only these observations: response times rose after deployment; no memory metrics, traces, or heap profiles were collected. The team suspects a memory leak. Name the cause if the evidence supports it; otherwise preserve the uncertainty.
criteria: Exactly two sentences suitable for an incident update.
Reports higher response times after deployment without asserting deployment causation as established.
Preserves the memory leak as a suspicion or unconfirmed hypothesis.
Makes the evidence limitation clear; does not invent memory growth, garbage-collection pauses, retained objects, profiling results, or a confirmed root cause.

cases.prompt: Write a warm, reassuring customer notice, 35 words maximum. Use ordinary complete sentences. Facts: some checkout attempts failed from 14:00 to 14:12 UTC; checkout now works; affected customers can try again. We haven't verified whether anyone was charged. Do not invent assurances or teach technical terms. Return only the notice.
criteria: Only a customer notice, at most 35 words, using warm ordinary complete sentences.
States that some checkout attempts failed during 14:00–14:12 UTC, checkout now works, and affected customers may try again.
Does not promise no charges, refunds, no duplicate payments, or that all customers were affected.
Avoids engineer-facing jargon and definitions. Do not force compressed fragments or conversational skill branding into the authored notice.
Explicitly discussing unverified charges is optional; any statement about them must preserve uncertainty.

cases.prompt: Tighten this runbook rule to at most 25 words. Preserve every condition and limit: 'Retry the request at most twice, only if the operation is idempotent and the server returned 503; never retry after the cancellation token is signaled.'
criteria: At most 25 words; punctuation and inline formatting are allowed.
Retains at most two retries, not two total attempts.
Both idempotence and an HTTP 503 response remain necessary conditions.
Cancellation overrides retry permission: no retry after the token is signaled.
Does not weaken "only if" to an example or suggestion, reverse idempotence, or omit the cancellation condition.
Does not add a definition of idempotence.

cases.prompt: Return only valid JSON with exactly these keys in this order: "status", "detail". status must be "timeout". Write detail as one precise sentence based only on: the caller stopped waiting after 5 seconds; we do not know whether the server completed the operation. Do not call this a server crash or a confirmed failure.
criteria: Parses as a JSON object with exactly two keys in source order: status, then detail; no Markdown fence or surrounding prose.
status is exactly the string "timeout".
detail is a single sentence stating that the caller stopped waiting after 5 seconds and server completion is unknown.
Does not equate client timeout with a crashed server, rolled-back operation, or confirmed operation failure.

cases.prompt: Copyedit this recipe instruction using the correct cooking term. Return one sentence, no definitions: 'Sauté the onions gently in butter until soft and translucent, without letting them brown.' The method must stay the same.
criteria: One recipe sentence; uses "sweat" or an equivalent established culinary expression for gently softening onions without browning.
Preserves onions, butter, gentle heat, softness/translucence, and no browning.
Does not alter the method to high-heat sautéing, caramelization, or frying until brown merely to fit the original verb.
No glossary or software analogy.

cases.prompt: Fix the terminology in this literary analysis, keeping its tentative interpretation and first-person voice: 'I think the author is unreliable: the fictional first-person speaker contradicts their earlier account, though the text does not establish whether this is deliberate deception.' No explanation; return the revised sentence.
criteria: Replaces the mistaken attribution to the author with narrator or equivalent accurate reference to the fictional first-person speaker.
Keeps first-person framing, tentative interpretation, the contradiction with an earlier account, and uncertainty about deliberate deception.
One revised sentence; no explanatory aside or lecture about unreliable narration.
Does not state that the writer personally lied or that contradiction proves intentional deceit.

cases.prompt: Review this release note for terminology errors. If it is already correct, return it unchanged, with no commentary: 'Optimistic concurrency control rejects an update when the stored version no longer matches the version read by the client.'
criteria: Returns the supplied release-note sentence verbatim, including its final period.
No label, quotation marks, formatting, definitions, or alternate implementation details.
Does not swap optimistic concurrency control for locking, serialization, or an unconditional guarantee against lost updates.

cases.prompt: Review this research caption for terminology errors. If it is already correct, return it unchanged, with no commentary: 'In this observational sample, longer sleep duration was associated with lower reported stress; the analysis does not establish causation.'
criteria: Returns the supplied research-caption sentence verbatim, including its punctuation.
No glossary, warning, commentary, or software metaphor.
Preserves observational scope, association, reported stress, and the explicit lack of established causation.

cases.prompt: Term-Inator, explain me what an ICP is.
criteria: Recognize that ICP has materially different domain meanings; ask a concise clarification instead of silently choosing one or supplying a long glossary. A short choice of meanings is acceptable as disambiguation, not unsolicited teaching.

cases.prompt: We sell payroll software to small companies. Term-Inator, explain me what an ICP is in two sentences.
criteria: Use ideal customer profile in the sales context and explain normally in two sentences. No unnecessary clarification, invented claims about the company's actual customer base, or conflation of a customer organization with a buyer persona.

cases.prompt: Term-Inator, explain EBITDA in two sentences using only this glossary entry: EBITDA stands for earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization. It is a financial performance measure; it is not cash flow.
criteria: Explain and expand EBITDA, retain the supplied exclusions, identify its performance-measure role and distinction from cash flow in two sentences. No refusal or suppression because the core skill is not a teaching workflow.

cases.prompt: Term-Inator, write one sentence for a business update using the correct terms. Existing customers kept their subscriptions, but some moved to cheaper plans, reducing the revenue from those customers. No definitions or recommendations.
criteria: Describe revenue contraction/downgrades without implying lost customers, invented revenue amounts, definitions, or advice; one sentence.

cases.prompt: Term-Inator, check this sentence for terminology errors; return it unchanged if accurate. In our billing domain, an 'account' is a customer organization, and a 'member' is a person belonging to one; these are intentional domain terms. Sentence: 'An account can have multiple members.'
criteria: Return `An account can have multiple members.` verbatim, with no forced replacement by tenant/user or extra commentary.

cases.prompt: Term-Inator, rewrite this for a nontechnical reader in one sentence, with no specialist terms: 'Authorization failed because the account lacks the required role.'
criteria: Honor the requested plain-language rewrite and preserve the access-permission failure; do not imply a wrong password or retain authorization/role jargon.

cases.prompt: Name the architectural pattern in one short sentence: our application represents state as an append-only sequence of domain events and reconstructs current state by replaying those events. Do not recommend implementation changes.
criteria: Identify event sourcing in one short sentence without an unsolicited definition, implementation recommendation, or claiming that the supplied behavior proves CQRS.

scoring: Score each case as pass or fail against every required criterion below. A pass requires both factual fidelity and the requested format; fluent wording alone is insufficient. Record the response and a short reason for any failure. Allow equivalent correct terms and natural wording unless a case explicitly requires unchanged text. Do not demand the example phrasing implied by a criterion. Global requirements: preserve facts, logical conditions, units, scope, uncertainty, and requested voice. Do not invent diagnoses, mechanisms, verification, or evidence. Do not append teaching, definitions, follow-up offers, or summaries when not requested. Explain normally when explanation is explicitly requested. Short wording must remain interpretable.
